quests.instruction: You get a single, perfect scoop of your favorite ice cream flavor exactly when you wanted it. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a bright, specific burst of joy about one small perfect moment, not a big feeling spread across a whole day.
quests.explanation: This is delighted rather than joyful — delighted fits one small, perfect moment, while joyful usually describes a bigger feeling spread across a whole event.
quests.funFact: Small perfect moments like this are a wonderful, easy way to feel a burst of happiness during an ordinary day!

quests.instruction: You are curled up at home with a warm blanket and nothing you need to do all afternoon. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a slow, settled kind of good feeling, not a big burst of energy.
quests.explanation: This is content rather than excited — content is a slow, settled kind of good feeling, while excited is a bigger burst of energy.
quests.funFact: Content is sometimes called the quiet cousin of happy — calm instead of bouncy!

quests.instruction: Your entire class surprises you with a party for your biggest achievement ever. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a much bigger version of happy — think about a whole class celebrating your biggest achievement together.
quests.explanation: This is ecstatic rather than proud — ecstatic is the huge burst of joy from the celebration itself, while proud focuses more on the achievement alone.
quests.funFact: Celebrating together as a whole class can make a joyful moment feel even bigger and more special!

quests.instruction: Someone steals credit for the project you did entirely on your own. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a much stronger version of angry — think about your whole effort being unfairly claimed by someone else.
quests.explanation: This is furious rather than angry — furious fits your whole effort being unfairly claimed by someone else.
quests.funFact: Calmly explaining what really happened to a teacher can help set the record straight.

quests.instruction: You are separated from your family in a massive, crowded place with no way to see them anywhere. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a much stronger version of scared — think about a huge crowd with absolutely no familiar face in sight.
quests.explanation: This is terrified rather than scared — terrified fits a huge crowd with no familiar face anywhere, a much bigger fear than a brief startle.
quests.funFact: Picking a clear meeting spot before going somewhere crowded is a smart family safety plan.

quests.instruction: You are the one chosen to carry the flag at the front of the school parade. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is feeling honored and good about being chosen, not the flutter of uncertainty.
quests.explanation: This is proud rather than nervous — proud is the honored, good feeling of being chosen, while nervous would be more about feeling unsure right before doing it.
quests.funFact: Being chosen for a special role like this is often remembered as a highlight of the whole year!

quests.instruction: You keep glancing at the door every few minutes, waiting for your dad to come home from his long work trip. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a bouncy, ready feeling focused on someone arriving soon, stronger than a simple wish for good news.
quests.explanation: This is eager rather than hopeful — eager is a bouncy, ready feeling about someone arriving very soon, while hopeful is more about wishing for good news in general.
quests.funFact: Counting down the hours is a common way this bouncy, ready feeling shows itself!

quests.instruction: You find out you get to go on the trip of your absolute dreams. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a much bigger version of excited — think about your single biggest dream trip actually happening.
quests.explanation: This is ecstatic rather than excited — ecstatic is an even bigger, overwhelming joy, fitting your biggest dream actually coming true.
quests.funFact: Planning out all the details ahead of time is a fun way to enjoy this huge, joyful feeling even longer!

quests.instruction: You discover someone has been reading your private journal without asking. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a much stronger version of angry — think about your privacy being deliberately invaded.
quests.explanation: This is furious rather than embarrassed — furious fits a deliberate invasion of your privacy, which is bigger than simple embarrassment.
quests.funFact: A private box or notebook lock is a simple way to help protect your own personal space.

quests.instruction: A huge, sudden storm knocks out all the lights while you are completely alone in your room. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a much stronger version of scared — think about sudden total darkness with no one else around.
quests.explanation: This is terrified rather than scared — terrified fits sudden total darkness with no one else around, a much bigger fear than a simple startle.
quests.funFact: Keeping a flashlight within reach is a smart way to feel more prepared if the lights ever go out suddenly.

quests.instruction: You keep telling your friends about the new scooter you earned by saving up your own allowance. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is about feeling good over earning or achieving something, not simply having a burst of energy about it.
quests.explanation: This is proud rather than excited — proud centers on feeling good about having earned or achieved something, while excited is more about anticipating something fun ahead.
quests.funFact: Sharing good news with friends is a natural part of feeling proud of something you worked for!

quests.instruction: You spend the entire day at your favorite theme park, riding every ride until the park closes. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a huge burst of joy from an amazing day, bigger than everyday happiness.
quests.explanation: This is ecstatic rather than happy — ecstatic describes a huge burst of joy from an amazing experience, stronger than everyday happiness.
quests.funFact: Days this thrilling are often remembered as some of the best of the whole year!

quests.instruction: Someone intentionally ruins the group project the whole team worked on for weeks. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a much stronger version of angry — think about a whole team's weeks of work being deliberately destroyed.
quests.explanation: This is furious rather than frustrated — furious fits deliberate destruction of a whole team's hard work, not just a repeating struggle.
quests.funFact: Working together to rebuild what was lost is a powerful way a team can bounce back stronger.

quests.instruction: You realize you are stuck at the very top of an extremely tall ride that has stopped moving. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a much stronger version of scared — think about being stuck very high up with no way down yet.
quests.explanation: This is terrified rather than nervous — terrified fits being stuck very high up unexpectedly, a much bigger fear than the flutter before a ride even begins.
quests.funFact: Ride operators are trained to get everyone down safely — being stuck briefly is a normal part of ride safety checks.

quests.instruction: Your team wins the championship after an entire season of hard work. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a much bigger version of happy — think about an entire season of effort paying off all at once.
quests.explanation: This is ecstatic rather than proud — ecstatic is the huge, overwhelming joy of the win itself, while proud focuses more on your own hard work paying off.
quests.funFact: Championship wins after a long season are often remembered as some of the most joyful team moments ever!

quests.instruction: Someone cheats to win the game after you played completely fairly the whole time. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a much stronger version of angry — think about unfairness that breaks the whole point of playing.
quests.explanation: This is furious rather than angry — furious fits unfairness so big it breaks the whole point of playing fair.
quests.funFact: Telling an adult calmly about cheating helps keep games fair for everyone next time.

quests.instruction: You hear a loud smoke alarm suddenly go off in the middle of the night. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a much stronger version of scared — think about a sudden, urgent alarm jolting you awake at night.
quests.explanation: This is terrified rather than scared — terrified fits the sudden, urgent jolt of an alarm at night, a much bigger fear than an everyday startle.
quests.funFact: Knowing your family's fire escape plan ahead of time can help you feel prepared, even in a scary moment like this.

quests.instruction: You get to meet your all-time favorite author in person. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a much bigger version of happy — think about meeting someone you have admired for a very long time.
quests.explanation: This is ecstatic rather than amazed — ecstatic is the huge burst of joy from meeting someone you admire, while amazed is more about astonishment alone.
quests.funFact: Meeting someone whose work has meant so much to you is a rare, thrilling kind of joy!

quests.instruction: Someone deliberately trips you on purpose in front of the whole class. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a much stronger version of angry — think about someone deliberately trying to hurt or embarrass you on purpose.
quests.explanation: This is furious rather than embarrassed — the deliberate, hurtful intent behind this makes it a much stronger feeling than simple embarrassment.
quests.funFact: Telling a teacher right away is the best next step whenever someone deliberately hurts you on purpose.

quests.instruction: An enormous, unfamiliar dog corners you, barking loudly, with no way to step back. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a much stronger version of scared — think about being cornered with nowhere to go.
quests.explanation: This is terrified rather than scared — terrified fits being cornered with nowhere to go, a much bigger fear than a simple startle.
quests.funFact: Standing very still and avoiding eye contact is what experts recommend if a dog like this ever happens.

quests.instruction: You find out you won first place in the biggest competition of your life. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a much bigger version of happy — think about the biggest win of your whole life so far.
quests.explanation: This is ecstatic rather than happy — ecstatic is a much bigger, more overwhelming joy, fitting a huge, life-highlight win like this.
quests.funFact: Moments this big are often remembered as some of the happiest memories of a person's whole life!

quests.instruction: Your little brother deliberately breaks the one toy you asked him never to touch. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a much hotter version of angry — think about a clear, deliberate rule being broken on purpose.
quests.explanation: This is furious rather than angry — furious fits a rule being broken deliberately and completely, not just an accidental mistake.
quests.funFact: Stepping away for a moment to cool down is a smart first step before talking through a big feeling like this.

quests.instruction: You are caught outside in a sudden, violent thunderstorm with nowhere to take shelter nearby. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a much stronger version of scared — think about being caught out in the open with no shelter in sight.
quests.explanation: This is terrified rather than scared — terrified fits being caught in the open with no shelter, a much bigger fear than an everyday startle.
quests.funFact: Crouching low in a ditch or low area, away from tall trees, is a safety tip for sudden storms outdoors.

quests.instruction: You find out your whole family is moving to the exact town you have always wanted to live in. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a much bigger version of happy — think about a long-held wish coming true all at once.
quests.explanation: This is ecstatic rather than hopeful — ecstatic fits a wish that has actually come true, going far beyond simply hoping for it.
quests.funFact: News this big often takes a little time to fully sink in, even after the huge excitement!

quests.instruction: You discover someone has been telling lies about you behind your back for weeks. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a much stronger version of angry — think about weeks of unfair lies, not just a single unfair moment.
quests.explanation: This is furious rather than angry — furious fits a bigger betrayal like weeks of lies, going beyond a single unfair incident.
quests.funFact: Talking calmly to a trusted adult is a strong first step when a problem like this feels too big to handle alone.

quests.instruction: You wake up in the middle of the night to a very loud, sudden thunderclap right overhead. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a much stronger version of scared — think about being jolted awake by an enormous, sudden sound.
quests.explanation: This is terrified rather than scared — terrified fits being jolted awake by an enormous, sudden sound, a much bigger fear than a regular startle.
quests.funFact: Thunder is loudest and most sudden when a storm is very close by — it moves away again quickly.

quests.instruction: You get accepted into the special program you have wanted to join forever. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a much bigger version of happy — think about a long-held dream finally coming true.
quests.explanation: This is ecstatic rather than happy — ecstatic fits a long-held dream finally coming true, going far beyond everyday happiness.
quests.funFact: Working toward a long-held goal often makes the moment it finally happens feel even more amazing!

quests.instruction: You find out your best friend shared your biggest secret with the entire class. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a much stronger version of angry — think about a big trust being broken in front of everyone.
quests.explanation: This is furious rather than disappointed — furious fits a big trust broken so completely, going beyond a simple letdown.
quests.funFact: Talking honestly about how much this hurt is an important step toward repairing a friendship.

quests.instruction: You are completely lost and alone in an unfamiliar place with no one in sight. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a much stronger version of scared — think about being truly alone with no familiar faces anywhere.
quests.explanation: This is terrified rather than scared — terrified is a much stronger, overwhelming fear, fitting being completely alone in an unfamiliar place.
quests.funFact: Staying in one place and looking for a helper, like a worker in a uniform, is the safest first step if this ever happens.

quests.instruction: You discover you got the leading role you have dreamed about since you started acting. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a much bigger version of happy — think about a long-held dream in acting finally coming true.
quests.explanation: This is ecstatic rather than hopeful — ecstatic fits a dream that has actually come true, going far beyond simply hoping for it.
quests.funFact: A dream role like this is often the reward for a long journey of practice and auditions!
